newsitem.title: ITALY: Gaddafi a "changed man", says Egpyt's Mubarak.
newsitem.headline: Gaddafi a "changed man", says Egpyt's Mubarak.

text.p: Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi is a changed man and sanctions against his country should be lifted, Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak was quoted as saying on Monday.
"Gaddafi today is a different man. You can cooperate with him," Mubarak told the Italian newspaper La Repubblica.
"If on the other hand you maintain the embargo you will push him back into isolation," he said in an interview.
The U.N. Security Council in 1992 imposed an arms and air embargo on Libya.

It took action to force Tripoli to hand over for trial two of its citizens suspected in the 1988 bombing of a Pan Am airliner over Lockerbie, Scotland in which 270 people died and to cooperate with a French probe over the 1989 mid-air bombing of a French UTA airliner in which 170 died.
Gaddafi says the trial would only be acceptable in a third country.

The Libyan leader had good words in an interview published on Monday for the leaders of two countries confronting him over the airliner bombings, calling U.S. President Bill Clinton "a good man", and French President Jacques Chirac courageous.
He told the French daily Le Figaro that Clinton, a Democrat, had been hampered by the Republicans' legacy in his first term but would have a free hand in the second term he has just won.
